name: Croatia
description: Croatia offers expats a desirable blend of Mediterranean lifestyle, stunning natural beauty, and a relatively lower cost of living compared to many Western European countries. Its high safety ratings and rich cultural heritage further enhance its appeal for those seeking a relaxed yet engaging European experience. The country's recent economic growth and EU membership also provide stability and opportunities.
longdescription: Expat life in Croatia is characterized by a slower, more relaxed pace, particularly in coastal regions, where coffee culture and outdoor activities are highly valued [3, 5]. The country boasts a beautiful coastline with over a thousand islands, rich forests, and historic cities, making it ideal for those who appreciate natural beauty and cultural heritage [3, 6, 22]. While the economy is significantly driven by tourism, especially in the summer months, which can lead to crowded conditions, there's also a growing IT sector and increasing interest from digital nomads [3, 8, 36]. Croatia consistently ranks among Europe's safest countries, offering a sense of peace and security for residents [3, 5, 6, 29, 30, 37]. Healthcare is generally of good quality, with universal coverage available for residents, though the public system can be strained [3, 11, 22]. The language, Croatian, can be challenging to learn due to its Slavic origin and complex grammar, but English is widely spoken in tourist areas and by younger generations [3, 6, 8, 11]. Bureaucracy can be cumbersome and slow, often requiring patience for administrative tasks like obtaining residence permits [3, 5, 6, 9, 29].

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Digital Nomads
visas.description: The Temporary Residence Permit for Digital Nomads in Croatia is designed for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens who perform remote work or provide services exclusively for non-Croatian entities. It allows individuals to live in Croatia for an extended period while benefiting from specific tax exemptions on their foreign-sourced income.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are remote workers, freelancers, or self-employed individuals who are citizens of non-EU/EEA/Swiss countries, derive their income from abroad, and do not intend to work for Croatian companies or clients.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This temporary residence permit does not lead to permanent residency or citizenship in Croatia.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit cannot be renewed consecutively. Applicants must leave Croatia for at least six months after their permit expires before they can apply for a new one.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the Digital Nomad Residence Permit are exempt from Croatian income tax on earnings derived from their remote work for foreign employers or clients. This exemption applies for the duration of the permit.
benefits: Exemption from Croatian income tax on foreign-sourced earnings.
Ability to reside in Croatia for up to 18 months.
Family reunification is permitted, allowing spouses, partners, and children to join.
Access to a country that is part of the Schengen Area and uses the Euro.
Fast and relatively straightforward application process.
required_documents: Completed application form (Form 1a or online submission)
Valid passport (valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay)
Passport-size photo (3 x 3.5 cm)
Proof of remote employment or business ownership outside Croatia (employment contract, service agreements, company registration)
Proof of sufficient financial means (bank statements showing consistent monthly income or lump-sum savings)
Proof of health insurance valid in Croatia for the entire duration of stay
Police clearance certificate (clean criminal record) from home country and any country of residence for over a year, legalized and translated if necessary
Proof of accommodation in Croatia (rental agreement, property deed, host confirmation)
Proof of paid administrative fees
application_process_steps: Gather all required documents, ensuring they are translated into Croatian or English if necessary.
Submit the application online via the Ministry of the Interior portal, at a Croatian embassy/consulate abroad, or in person at a local police administration in Croatia if legally present.
Pay the applicable administrative and processing fees.
Wait for the application to be processed and for approval.
If required, obtain a long-term (D) visa from a Croatian embassy or consulate to enter Croatia.
Upon arrival or approval, register your temporary address with the local police within three days and collect your biometric residence card.

visas.name: Temporary Stay and Work Permit (Employed Worker Permit)
visas.description: The Temporary Stay and Work Permit (Employed Worker Permit) in Croatia is a single permit allowing non-EU/EEA citizens to temporarily reside and work in Croatia for a specific employer. This permit is granted based on an employment contract with a Croatian company and typically requires a labor market test to ensure no suitable local or EU/EEA candidates are available.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA citizens) who have secured a job offer and signed an employment contract with a registered Croatian employer.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Work-based temporary residence is a reliable route to permanent residence. After 5 years of continuous legal residence on a temporary permit (with limited absences), individuals become eligible to apply for permanent residence. Permanent residency can then lead to eligibility for Croatian citizenship through naturalization, typically requiring 8 years of continuous legal residence in total.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain employment with the same employer (or obtain approval for change after one year in the same occupational field). Application for renewal must be submitted no later than 30 days before the expiry of the valid permit. A basic Croatian language test may be required for renewal.
benefits: Allows legal employment and temporary residence in Croatia.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency after 5 years of continuous legal stay.
Enables family reunification, allowing dependants to apply for temporary residence.
Longer initial validity period, up to 3 years for permits requiring Croatian Employment Service opinion.
required_documents: Copy of valid travel document (passport, valid for at least 3 months beyond intended stay).
Color photograph (30x35 mm or 35x45 mm).
Evidence of adequate means of supporting oneself.
Evidence of health insurance valid in Croatia.
Proof of no criminal convictions from home country or country of residence for the last year (for first permit, duly legalized).
Employment contract or other relevant contract with a Croatian employer.
Proof of academic qualifications and professional skills (with official translations if required).
Evidence of the employer's registration in Croatia.
Employer declaration confirming adequate accommodation (Form 17a).
Certificate of health and vaccination status (Form 18a, if required by new rules).
application_process_steps: Secure a valid job offer and employment contract from a Croatian employer.
The employer initiates a labor market test with the Croatian Employment Service (HZZ) to confirm no suitable local or EU/EEA candidates, if required.
Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and translated into Croatian.

The employer or employee submits the application for a stay and work permit to the competent police administration/station in Croatia, or to a Croatian diplomatic mission/consular office abroad if a visa is required for entry.
Pay the administrative fees for the permit decision and biometric residence card.

Authorities review the application, and if approved, the employee provides biometric data and collects the residence permit card. If a visa is required, apply for a long-term (D) visa after approval, enter Croatia, register address, and then collect the permit card.

visas.name: EU Blue Card
visas.description: The EU Blue Card in Croatia is a combined residence and work permit for highly qualified non-EU citizens. It allows professionals to live and work legally in Croatia in highly skilled positions, offering a streamlined path to long-term EU residence and family reunification.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals with a university degree or equivalent higher education qualification (or recognized professional experience in certain ICT roles) who have a binding job offer or work contract in Croatia for at least one year in a highly qualified position that meets the national salary threshold.
visas.path_to_residency_description: An EU Blue Card holder can apply for long-term EU residence status after five years of continuous legal stay within the EU, provided at least two of those years were spent in Croatia. This path can eventually lead to Croatian citizenship by naturalization after a certain period of continuous residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: A request for renewal must be submitted at least 30 days before the current permit expires. Conditions include maintaining income threshold, valid health insurance, and a valid travel document. The applicant is allowed to stay in Croatia while their renewal application is being processed.
benefits: Live and work legally in Croatia for the duration of the contract (plus up to three additional months), extended up to 4 years.
Change employers after a certain period, with notification or approval from Croatian authorities.
Facilitated family reunification for close family members.
Mobility to other EU countries under certain conditions after 12-18 months of residence.
Pathway to long-term EU residence status after five years of continuous legal stay within the EU (with at least two years in Croatia).
required_documents: Completed application form for temporary stay and work of a highly qualified third-country national (EU Blue Card)
Valid passport (must be valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay)
Recent passport-size photographs (two, in color, meeting biometric standards)
Employment contract or binding job offer valid for at least one year, issued by a Croatian employer, specifying a gross annual salary meeting the threshold

Proof of higher education qualifications (university diploma or equivalent) and recognition if required, or proof of at least three years of professional experience (in the past seven years) in the IT sector for certain roles
Proof of accommodation in Croatia (rental agreement, property ownership, or employer-provided housing)
Proof of health insurance covering the applicant in Croatia
Clean criminal record certificate (from home country or country of residence, usually not older than six months)
application_process_steps: Ensure your employment contract is valid for at least one year, for a highly skilled position, and meets the minimum gross annual salary threshold.
Gather all required documents, including passport, photographs, employment contract, proof of qualifications, accommodation, health insurance, and a clean criminal record certificate.
Submit your application either at a Croatian diplomatic mission or consular post abroad, or at a local police administration office (MUP) in Croatia if already legally present.
Provide biometric data (fingerprints and signature) and pay the required administrative fees.
Wait for approval, with typical processing times between 30-60 days.
Upon approval, collect your biometric residence permit and report your residence to the police administration/station within 30 days.

visas.name: Posted Worker Permit
visas.description: The 'Posted Worker Program' in Croatia facilitates the temporary assignment of employees by foreign companies to perform services within Croatia. It ensures that posted workers benefit from minimum Croatian labor standards, including remuneration, working hours, and health and safety, while maintaining social security coverage from their home country if applicable. The requirements vary based on the worker's nationality and the employer's country of establishment, particularly regarding the need for a temporary stay permit.
visas.target_applicant: Workers legally employed by a foreign employer (from an EEA/Swiss Confederation member state or a third country) who are sent to Croatia for a limited period to provide services.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Time spent in Croatia under a posting does not count towards eligibility for permanent residency.
visas.renewal_conditions: The A1 Certificate and temporary stay permit (if applicable) require extension if the assignment period is prolonged.
visas.tax_implications: Tax implications depend on national laws and double tax agreements between the worker's home country and Croatia. If an A1 certificate is valid, the employee generally remains covered under their home country's social security system; otherwise, Croatian social security rules apply.
benefits: Guaranteed minimum working conditions as per Croatian legislation, including minimum wage, working hours, rest periods, and annual leave.
Social security coverage typically maintained in the home country with an A1 certificate (for EU/EEA/Swiss nationals).
Allows temporary work in Croatia without requiring a specific work permit for EU/EEA/Swiss nationals.
Streamlined process for third-country nationals posted from an EU/EEA employer for up to 90 days.
No labor market test required for residence and work permits for third-country nationals posted from a third-country employer under international agreements.
required_documents: A1 Certificate (or S1 form/European health insurance card for healthcare).
Work contract with the employer (service provider).
Individual pay list and pay statement.
Identification card.
For third-country nationals: valid work and residence permit in the employer's home state.
Posting declaration (submitted by the employer).
Records of working hours (to be kept by the employer).
application_process_steps: Foreign employer submits a prior posting declaration electronically to the Croatian Labour Inspectorate (or Ministry of Labour and Pension System) before the commencement of services.
Employer designates a liaison/contact person in Croatia.
Worker obtains an A1 Certificate (or equivalent) from their home country's social security authority to confirm social security coverage.
For third-country nationals posted from an EU/EEA employer for more than 90 days: apply for temporary residence for the purpose of work of a posted worker.
For third-country nationals posted from a third-country employer under international agreements: apply for a residence and work permit without a labor market test.
Any changes to the provided data in the posting declaration must be reported by the employer within 3 days.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Self-Employment (Business Temporary Residence Permit)
visas.description: This permit allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens to reside in Croatia for the purpose of self-employment by establishing and actively managing a Croatian company or sole proprietorship. It requires demonstrating genuine economic activity and a significant contribution to the local economy.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a non-EU/EEA/Swiss entrepreneur who plans to establish and operate a legitimate business in Croatia, actively managing it as its director or owner.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five continuous years of temporary residence in Croatia, the permit holder becomes eligible to apply for permanent residency. Continuous residence implies limited absences (up to 10 months over five years or two months per year).
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit can be renewed if the applicant continues to meet the conditions under which it was originally granted, including maintaining the required investment, employment of Croatian citizens, and personal income. An application for extension must be submitted no later than 30 days before the expiry of the current permit.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this permit are subject to standard Croatian tax laws for residents on their worldwide income, as they are actively engaged in a Croatian business. No special tax exemptions are specified for this category.
benefits: Permission to live and work legally in Croatia through one's own business.
Opportunity for family reunification, allowing spouses and children to join the permit holder.
Provides a pathway to permanent residency in Croatia after five years of continuous temporary residence.
Allows full integration into the Croatian economic and social system as a resident entrepreneur.
required_documents: Valid passport (valid at least 3 months beyond intended stay)
Color passport photographs (30x35mm or 3x3.5cm)
Proof of health insurance
Proof of sufficient financial means to support oneself and any dependents
Criminal background check certificate (not older than 6 months, duly legalized for first permit)
Proof of accommodation in Croatia (e.g., rental agreement, property ownership, notarized statement from host)
Company registration documents (e.g., extract from Commercial Court Registry)
Proof of business activity and economic viability (e.g., business plan, investment receipts)
Proof of investment of at least HRK 200,000.00 in the company or sole trade
Copies of employment contracts and registrations for pension and statutory health insurance for at least three Croatian nationals
List of shareholders certified by the Commercial Court or a notary's certificate (for d.o.o.)
Completed application form (Form 2a)
Certified translations into Croatian for foreign documents
application_process_steps: Legally form a company (d.o.o.) or register a sole proprietorship (obrt) in Croatia.
Gather all required documents, including financial proof, health insurance, criminal record, and company registration details.

Submit the application for temporary residence at the competent Croatian diplomatic mission/consular office abroad or at a local police administration/station in Croatia (if visa-exempt or legally residing).
Attend any required appointments, interviews, or biometrics sessions at the police administration/station.
Pay the application fees and the fee for the biometric residence card upon approval.
Register your residential address at the local police administration/station within three days of entering Croatia or receiving the permit.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Study (Higher Education)
visas.description: This permit is for non-EU/EEA citizens accepted into a higher education institution in Croatia, allowing them to reside legally in the country for study programs lasting longer than 90 days. It serves as a temporary residence permit specifically for academic purposes.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA citizens who have received an official acceptance or enrollment letter from a recognized Croatian university, faculty, or polytechnic institution for a program exceeding 90 days.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Temporary residence for study partially counts towards the eligibility requirements for permanent residence in Croatia. The exact duration and conditions for transitioning to permanent residency after studies would require further specific applications under other categories (e.g., employment).
visas.renewal_conditions: Must remain enrolled in a Croatian higher education institution and continue to meet all visa and financial conditions. Proof of continued enrollment and updated proof of funds are required for renewal applications.
benefits: Allows legal residence in Croatia for the duration of studies.
Can be renewed annually as long as academic enrollment and other conditions are met.
Provides a pathway that partially counts towards permanent residency in Croatia.
Enables access to student services and facilities in Croatia.
required_documents: Completed application form for temporary residence (Form 1a for non-EU citizens)
Valid passport (must be valid for at least three months beyond intended stay and issued within the last 10 years)
Letter of acceptance or enrollment certificate from a Croatian higher education institution

Proof of sufficient financial means (e.g., bank statement showing at least €620 per month or €7,440 per year, scholarship confirmation, or sponsor letter, or a lump sum of at least €3,500 for an academic year, plus €800 for return travel costs).
Proof of accommodation (e.g., dormitory confirmation, rental agreement, or private housing contract)
Valid health insurance coverage for Croatia (minimum €30,000 coverage).
Criminal background check from home country (not older than six months, apostilled or legalized if issued abroad).
One recent color passport-sized photo (30x35mm or 35x45mm).
Parental authorization if the applicant is a minor.
application_process_steps: Obtain an official letter of acceptance or enrollment from a recognized Croatian higher education institution.
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are translated into Croatian and apostilled/legalized if issued abroad.

Submit the application for temporary residence either at the nearest Croatian diplomatic mission/consulate in your home country (prior to arrival) or, in certain cases, at the appropriate police department/station in Croatia upon arrival.
Pay the application fees (temporary stay fee, biometric residence permit fee, and administrative fee).
Await processing of the application.
Once approved, provide biometric data at a police station and collect your biometric residence permit.
Register your residence and address with the local authorities within 3 days of entering Croatia if not handled by your accommodation provider.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Study (Secondary Education)
visas.description: The Temporary Residence Permit for Study (Secondary Education) in Croatia is for non-EU/EEA citizens who plan to enroll and study at an accredited Croatian secondary school for programs lasting longer than 90 days. This permit allows the holder to legally reside in Croatia for the purpose of their secondary education.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA citizens, typically minors aged 14 to 18, who have been accepted into a recognized Croatian secondary education institution.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Continuous legal temporary residence in Croatia for five years can lead to eligibility for permanent residency, provided all conditions under Croatian immigration law are met.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must remain enrolled in a recognized secondary education institution and continue to meet all temporary residence conditions.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Croatia for the duration of secondary studies
Permit is renewable annually for the length of the academic program
Access to local services and amenities during the stay
required_documents: Completed application form for temporary residence (Form 1a)
Valid passport or travel document (valid for at least 3 months beyond the intended stay)
Letter of acceptance or enrollment certificate from a recognized Croatian secondary school
Parental or legal guardian consent to study and reside in Croatia (for minors)
Proof of accommodation (student dormitory confirmation, host family agreement, or rental contract)
Proof of sufficient financial means (e.g., bank statement, sponsor letter from parents/guardians)
Health insurance coverage valid in Croatia
Certificate confirming no criminal convictions from home country and country of permanent residence (not older than 6 months)
One color passport-sized photograph (35x45 mm or 3x3.5 cm)
Originals or certified copies of all documents, with foreign documents translated into Croatian and certified
application_process_steps: Receive an official letter of acceptance or enrollment from a recognized Croatian secondary school.
Gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are translated into Croatian and certified.

Submit the completed application form (Form 1a) and supporting documents to the competent Croatian diplomatic mission/consular office in your home country, or to a police administration/station in Croatia if visa-exempt or under specific exceptions.
Pay the required administrative fees for temporary stay and the biometric residence permit.
Await processing and approval of the application by the Ministry of the Interior (MUP).

If approved, provide biometric data at the competent police administration/station to obtain the biometric residence permit card and register your address within three days of entering Croatia or changing residence.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Family Reunification
visas.description: This permit allows third-country nationals, who are close family members, to join a sponsor who is legally residing in Croatia. It provides a legal pathway for families to live together, ensuring access to health insurance, education, and potentially work opportunities in Croatia.
visas.target_applicant: Close family members (spouses, common-law partners, minor children, and parents of minor Croatian citizens or long-term residents/asylees) of Croatian citizens or third-country nationals holding valid temporary, permanent, or long-term residence in Croatia.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five continuous years of legal temporary stay in Croatia, holders of this permit may qualify for long-term or permanent residence. This status can eventually lead to eligibility for Croatian citizenship, subject to language and integration requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: The sponsor must continue to meet the legal conditions for family reunification, including valid residence, stable income, suitable accommodation, and health insurance. Renewal applications should be submitted no later than 30 to 60 days before the permit's expiration date.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of a temporary stay permit are generally subject to standard Croatian tax rules as residents. It is highly recommended to consult a local tax advisor for specific guidance on reporting requirements for bank accounts, property ownership, or other taxable assets.
benefits: Legally reside in Croatia with the sponsoring family member.
Access health insurance and education under similar conditions as other residents.
Ability to apply for a work permit (spouses of Croatian citizens and certain other categories can work without a separate work permit).
Renew or extend your stay as long as your sponsor's residence status remains valid.
Potential path to long-term or permanent residence after five continuous years of legal stay.
required_documents: Completed application form for temporary stay (Form 1a, available at MUP offices or online).
Valid travel document (passport), valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay.
Recent passport-size color photographs (typically 35x45 mm, white background).
Proof of family relationship (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate, or proof of common-law partnership).
Proof of legal residence of the sponsor in Croatia (e.g., copy of residence permit or Croatian ID).
Proof of accommodation in Croatia (e.g., rental contract, ownership deed, or letter of guarantee).
Proof of sufficient financial means to support the family (not required for family members of Croatian citizens or those granted asylum/subsidiary protection).
Proof of health insurance (not required for immediate family members of those granted asylum/subsidiary protection).
application_process_steps: Confirm eligibility by verifying family relationship and sponsor's legal status in Croatia.
Gather all necessary documentation, including application form, passport, photos, proof of relationship, accommodation, financial means (if applicable), and health insurance (if applicable).

Submit the application in person at a Croatian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad, or at a police administration/station in Croatia if the applicant does not require a visa to enter Croatia.
Pay the applicable administrative fees for the temporary stay application and the biometric residence permit card.
Attend any requested interviews or provide additional information as required by the authorities.
Await the decision on the application and, if approved, receive the temporary residence permit and biometric residence card.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Other Purposes (including passive income / retirement based on financial means or property ownership)
visas.description: This temporary residence permit is designed for non-EU/EEA citizens who wish to reside in Croatia for purposes other than employment, study, or family reunification, typically based on demonstrating sufficient financial means or property ownership. It functions as a de facto retirement or passive income visa, allowing a stay longer than 90 days.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are financially independent retirees, individuals with passive income from abroad, or those who own property in Croatia, seeking a long-term stay without engaging in local employment.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five continuous years of legal temporary residence in Croatia, third-country nationals may apply for permanent residency. Continuous residence implies no more than 10 months of total absence from Croatia over the five years, or no single absence longer than six consecutive months. A basic knowledge of Croatian language may also be required.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable annually, provided the applicant continues to meet the original conditions for its issuance, including maintaining sufficient financial means, valid health insurance, and proof of accommodation. Renewal applications should be submitted to the local police administration/station no later than 30-60 days before the current permit's expiry.
visas.tax_implications: Becoming a tax resident in Croatia is generally triggered by spending more than 183 days per year in the country or having a permanent home available for exclusive use. Croatian tax residents are potentially liable for taxes on their worldwide income. It is highly recommended to consult a tax professional for specific advice based on individual circumstances and to understand double taxation agreements.
benefits: Legal residency in Croatia for up to one year, renewable annually.
Potential path to permanent residency after five years of continuous legal stay.
Ability to reside in Croatia and access certain public services.
Freedom of movement within the Schengen Zone for up to 90 days within any 180-day period.
required_documents: Valid passport or travel document (valid for at least three months beyond the intended stay).
Completed application form (Obrazac 1a for non-EU citizens).
Two recent passport-sized photos (30x35 mm or 35x45 mm).
Proof of sufficient financial means for maintenance (e.g., bank statements, pension statements, confirmation of earnings).
Proof of assured accommodation in Croatia (e.g., rental contract, property ownership document, notarized statement from a host).
Proof of health insurance valid in Croatia.
Certificate confirming no criminal convictions from the home country and any country of permanent residence for the last year (apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Croatian).
Evidence supporting the grounds for residence permit (e.g., proof of property ownership if applicable for the 'other purposes' justification).
Birth and marriage certificates (if applicable, apostilled/legalized and translated).
application_process_steps: Determine eligibility and gather all required documents, ensuring foreign documents are apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Croatian.
Submit the application in person at a Croatian diplomatic mission or consular office abroad (if a visa is required to enter Croatia).
Alternatively, if visa-exempt, submit the application in person at the competent police administration/station (MUP) in Croatia according to the intended place of stay.
Attend any required appointments, interviews, or biometric data collection sessions (fingerprints and photograph).
Pay the applicable administrative fees for the temporary stay approval and the biometric residence card.
Receive the decision on the application and, if approved, collect the biometric residence card.
Register the residential address with the local police administration/station within three days of entering Croatia or receiving the permit.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit for Scientific Research
visas.description: This permit allows third-country nationals to temporarily reside in Croatia for the purpose of scientific research. It enables researchers to conduct their work and potentially teach at the host research institution without requiring a separate work permit.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens) who have secured a hosting agreement with a research organization in Croatia for scientific research.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years of uninterrupted legal temporary stay in Croatia, third-country nationals may apply for long-term residence. Uninterrupted stay allows for absences of up to 10 months in total over the five years, or a single absence not exceeding 6 months.
visas.renewal_conditions: The permit is renewable, provided the conditions for granting the temporary stay continue to be met. An application for extension must be submitted to the competent police administration/police station no later than 60 days (or at least 30 days) before the expiration of the current permit.
benefits: Legal residence in Croatia for the duration of the research.
Ability to teach at the host research facility without needing an additional residence and work permit.
Access to public health care after registration as a foreign national.
Freedom of movement within the Schengen Zone for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
Allows family members (spouse and children) to join on dependent visas.
Provides a pathway to long-term residency in Croatia after five years.
required_documents: Completed application form (Form 1a)
Valid travel document (passport) - original and copy, valid for at least three months longer than the requested residence period
Colour photograph (3x3.5 cm or 30x35 mm)
Proof of secured means of subsistence (e.g., hosting agreement, employment contract, or employer confirmation of salary)
Proof of health insurance

Proof that the applicant has not been convicted by a final ruling of any criminal offences in their home country or a country where they resided for more than one year immediately prior to arriving in Croatia (for first permit, duly legalised, unless exempt due to EU mobility programs)
Hosting agreement with a research organization in Croatia (original and copy)
Commercial court excerpt for the host institution (if applicable)
Approval of a scientific visit or accreditation for hosting foreign researchers (copy)
application_process_steps: Obtain a hosting agreement with an accredited research organization in Croatia.
Gather all required documents, including valid passport, proof of subsistence, health insurance, criminal record check, and the hosting agreement.

Submit the application (Form 1a) in person at a Croatian diplomatic mission or consular office in the applicant's country of origin, or at a police administration/station in Croatia if legally present (e.g., visa-free entry, or specific visa exceptions apply for researchers).
Pay the administrative fee for granting temporary stay (EUR 46.45) and the fee for the biometric residence permit (EUR 31.85 for normal procedure, plus an additional EUR 9.29 for issuance).
If the application is approved, appear at the competent police administration/police station to provide biometric data (fingerprints and photo) for the residence permit card.
Report the temporary residence address to the competent police administration/police station within three days of entering Croatia or changing address.

visas.name: Long-Term Residence
visas.description: Long-Term Residence (Dugotrajno boravište) in Croatia is a status granted to third-country nationals who have legally resided in the Republic of Croatia for an uninterrupted period of five years. It grants the right to live and work indefinitely in Croatia, serving as a crucial step towards full integration and potential Croatian citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU/EEA nationals who have maintained continuous legal temporary residence in Croatia for five years under various permits (e.g., work, family reunification, study), demonstrating stable financial means, accommodation, and basic Croatian language skills.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Long-Term Residence (Dugotrajno boravište) is synonymous with Permanent Stay (Stalni boravak) for third-country nationals and is the final legal step before becoming eligible to apply for Croatian citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The long-term residence status itself is indefinite, but the physical biometric residence card must be renewed every 5 or 10 years. Conditions for maintaining the status include not residing outside the EEA for 12 consecutive months, not being absent from Croatia for more than six years, and not posing a threat to public policy, national security, or public health.
benefits: Indefinite right to live in Croatia without annual renewals of temporary permits.
Right to work in Croatia without needing a separate work permit.
Final legal step before eligibility for Croatian citizenship.
Access to public services and social benefits similar to Croatian citizens.
Increased stability and integration into Croatian society.
required_documents: Completed application form (Form 1a)
Valid passport (valid for at least three months beyond planned stay)
Color passport-sized photos (e.g., 3x3.5 cm or 30x35mm/35x45mm)
Proof of continuous legal residence in Croatia for five years (e.g., previous temporary residence permits, registrations)
Proof of sufficient financial means to support oneself (e.g., bank statements, employment contracts, pension slips from the previous year)
Proof of accommodation in Croatia
Health insurance certificate (e.g., from HZZO for Croatian health insurance)

Criminal record certificate from home country (and any country of residence for over one year prior to Croatia, issued no more than 6 months prior, apostilled/legalized and officially translated into Croatian)
Croatian language and Latin script proficiency certificate (A1 level, with exemptions for age/education in Croatia)
application_process_steps: Complete five years of continuous legal temporary residence in Croatia, ensuring absences do not exceed 6 months in a single trip or 10 months total over the five-year period.
Maintain legal status and compliance throughout the five-year period.
Pass a Croatian language and Latin script exam (A1 level), unless exempt.
Gather all required documents, ensuring non-Croatian documents are officially translated by a court interpreter.
Submit the application (Form 1a) in person at the local police administration (Policijska uprava) or police station (Policijska postaja) responsible for your place of residence.
Wait for the Ministry of the Interior (MUP) to process the application and make a decision, which typically takes between 6 and 18 months.
Receive your permanent residence card upon approval.

visas.name: Permanent Stay (Permanent Residence)
visas.description: The Permanent Stay (Permanent Residence) program in Croatia grants foreign nationals, primarily third-country nationals, the right to live and work indefinitely within the Republic of Croatia. It is a status earned after an extended period of legal temporary residence, offering long-term stability and serving as a crucial step towards Croatian citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are third-country nationals who have legally and continuously resided in Croatia for five years under a qualifying temporary residence permit, or certain family members of Croatian or EU/EEA citizens with shorter residency periods.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Permanent Stay is the highest form of residency and allows for indefinite stay. After eight years of continuous legal residence in Croatia (including the period of temporary and permanent stay), an individual may be eligible to apply for Croatian citizenship, provided they demonstrate fluent Croatian language skills and full cultural integration.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of Permanent Stay in Croatia are considered tax residents and are subject to standard Croatian tax laws on their worldwide income. No specific preferential tax treatment is mentioned for this category.
benefits: Right to live and work in Croatia indefinitely without annual renewals.
Access to social welfare and public services similar to Croatian citizens.
Stability and long-term security in Croatia.
Serves as the final legal step before eligibility for Croatian citizenship.
Allows for family reunification.
required_documents: Completed application form (Form 1a for third-country nationals, Form 3b for EU/EEA family members).
Valid passport or ID (and a copy) valid for at least three months beyond the intended period of residence.
Recent color biometric passport photograph (30x35mm or 35x45mm).
Proof of continuous legal residence in Croatia for the required period (e.g., previous temporary residence permits, address registrations).
Proof of sufficient financial means to support oneself and dependants without relying on Croatian social assistance.
Valid Croatian or internationally recognized health insurance.
Proof of suitable accommodation in Croatia (e.g., title deed, lease contract, owner's consent certified by a notary or signed at MUP).
Certificate of passing the Croatian language and Latin script exam (A1 level), unless legally exempt.
Criminal background check from the applicant's home country, translated into Croatian and apostilled/legalized.
Birth and marriage certificates, where applicable, translated and legalized.
Proof of payment of administrative fees.
application_process_steps: Ensure you meet the continuous legal residence requirement (typically 5 years for third-country nationals, with specific absence limits: not exceeding 10 months total or 6 months consecutively within the 5-year period). Exceptions apply for certain family members and returning emigrants.

Gather all required documentation, including application form (Form 1a or 3b), valid passport, photos, proof of continuous residence, financial means, health insurance, accommodation, and a clean criminal record.
Prepare for and pass the Croatian language and culture exam (A1 level), unless exempted.
Submit the completed application form and all supporting documents in person to the local police administration (MUP) or police station competent for your place of temporary residence in Croatia.
Await the decision from the Ministry of the Interior, which typically takes between 6 to 18 months for long-term residence.
Upon approval, apply for and obtain your biometric permanent residence card (boravišna iskaznica) for an additional fee.

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Croatian citizenship by descent (jus sanguinis) is primarily based on having at least one parent who is a Croatian citizen at the time of your birth [13, 41]. It can also be acquired if you have a direct ancestor (parent, grandparent, great-grandparent, or even earlier emigrant) who was a Croatian citizen and permanently left Croatia before October 8, 1991, without renouncing their citizenship [10, 12, 13, 14, 27, 33]. There is no limit to how many generations back one can go, provided the unbroken chain of descent and emigration can be proven [10, 12]. Required documents typically include birth certificates of ancestors, proof of emigration, a criminal record check, and identity documents, often needing to be apostilled and translated [10, 12, 27, 33].

Naturalization.desc: Naturalization is an option for foreign nationals who have made Croatia their home. General requirements include being at least 18 years old, being released from foreign citizenship (or proving this will happen upon acquiring Croatian citizenship), and having a period of continuous legal residence in Croatia [10]. The standard requirement is at least eight years of continuous legal residence with a permanent residence permit [10, 39]. Applicants also need to demonstrate language proficiency in Croatian and an understanding of Croatian culture and its social system [10].

Birthright.desc: Croatian citizenship by birthright (jus soli) applies to a child born in Croatia if at least one of their parents is a Croatian citizen at the time of birth [13, 41]. A child found in Croatia whose parents are unknown or of unknown citizenship also acquires Croatian citizenship [13, 41]. This citizenship may cease if, by their fourteenth birthday, both parents are confirmed to be foreign citizens [41].

Spouse and Family.desc: Spouses of Croatian citizens can apply for naturalization. If your spouse is acquiring citizenship through descent (Article 11), you may also apply without meeting standard residence or language requirements [12]. Generally, marriage to a Croatian citizen is a path to naturalization, often with a shorter residency requirement compared to standard naturalization, but specific conditions apply [39, 42]. For children, if born outside Croatia to at least one Croatian citizen parent, citizenship can be acquired by registering them before they turn 18, or by the individual themselves between 18 and 21 years of age [42].

tax_advice:
- **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** Croatia operates a progressive personal income tax system with rates determined by municipalities and cities, typically ranging from approximately 15% to 23% for lower income bands and 25% to 33% for higher income bands [7, 17, 20, 24]. The exact rates depend on the individual's place of residence [7, 17, 20]. Since January 1, 2024, municipal surtaxes were abolished and replaced by these flexible local rates [20]. Default national rates of roughly 20% (lower band) and 30% (higher band) apply if a municipality does not set its own [20]. Residents are taxed on worldwide income, while non-residents are taxed only on Croatian-source income [7, 24]. A basic personal allowance of €600 per month (€7,200 annually) applies for 2026 [24]. Capital income (dividends, interest, capital gains) is generally subject to a flat tax rate of 12%, with some exceptions [7, 24]. Employee pension contributions are typically 20% [24].
- **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):** The standard corporate income tax rate is 18%. A reduced rate of 10% applies to companies with annual revenues up to €1,000,000 [15, 23, 26, 32]. Resident companies are taxed on their worldwide income, while non-resident companies are taxed only on Croatian-source income [15, 21, 23].
- **Value-Added Tax (VAT):** The standard VAT rate in Croatia is 25% [2, 16, 18, 19, 25]. Reduced rates of 13% apply to services like accommodation, certain foodstuffs, and utilities [2, 18, 19, 25]. A 5% reduced rate applies to items such as books, medicines, and daily newspapers [2, 18, 19, 25]. A 0% rate applies to certain international transport services, intra-EU supplies to VAT-registered buyers, and specific solar panel installations [2, 18, 25].
local_tips:
- **Cost of Living:** The cost of living varies significantly by location, with coastal hotspots like Split and Dubrovnik being more expensive, especially in summer [3, 5]. Overall, it is generally lower than in many Western European countries, particularly for groceries, utilities, and dining out [5, 6, 8, 31].
- **Language:** Croatian is the official language. While English is widely spoken in tourist areas and by younger generations, learning basic Croatian is highly recommended for long-term integration and dealing with official procedures [3, 5, 6, 8, 11]. Croatians are often patient and friendly towards those attempting to learn their language [3].
- **Safety:** Croatia is considered one of the safest countries in Europe, with a low violent crime rate [3, 5, 6, 29, 30, 31, 37]. Petty crime, such as pickpocketing, can occur in crowded tourist areas, so it's advisable to be vigilant and secure valuables [4, 35, 37].
- **Registration:** Non-EU nationals generally need to obtain a long-term residence permit after 90 days [3]. The process can involve cumbersome bureaucracy and significant paperwork, often requiring patience and multiple visits to government offices [3, 5, 9]. Certificates for birth, marriage, etc., may need to have an issue date of fewer than six months [9].
